annotations.text:
What disagrees today.

Decision 103 gave every menu one container and the interiors still speak three dialects. The zone and account panels set rows in the HUD's 12-point mono capitals; settings speaks the menu face at 17, sentence case; the ship panel is a third anatomy with two heads stacked and its own row height.

Grounds sit at four opacities (stops .6, panels .72, the old lists .96, the card on none), rules at four alphas, the two scroll thumbs disagree, and the log-in card is the one surface with no glass behind it at all.

None of it was decided; each was written by whoever wrote the page.

The language, in one breath.

Everything is a panel; a panel is rows; a row is one shape. One glass, one edge, one head, one band, one wash pair, one breathing key.

The menu speaks in the menu face at 17, sentence case; it reads in the mono at 12; it quotes names raw. Capitals belong to the HUD and the small labels.

A row's right end is what the row does: opens, reads, steps, fills, switches, or walks. Six ends spell every menu in the game.

Every number is the shipped one: the type ladder 12-14-17-21, the washes .18 and .07, the 44-point touch floor, the 560 cap, the 14-point margin.

The one open choice: the voice of a list.

The games and account lists inherited the HUD's register; settings has always spoken the menu's. This proposal gives every row the menu's voice, because a full-screen panel is read rather than glanced at, and 12-point capitals across 560 points is an instrument label stretched into a sentence.

The alternative board keeps today's HUD voice on the zone panel so the two can be judged side by side rather than by argument.

What adopting costs in code: the landing's lists take stage_row's vocabulary, the ship pager becomes the walker row under one head, and the log-in card becomes a stacked panel with the breathing key at its foot.
